title: Build the nightly stock file in time

blocks.text: Every night the warehouse sends its stock to a partner as one CSV file. The partner's importer reads the first line as the header and every following line as a record, and it rejects a file that has an empty line anywhere, the end included. The catalogue was 2,000 items when the export was written; next quarter it will be 300,000, and the export has to finish in the same window.

`StockExport` already formats one record with `line(item)`. Write `csv(items)` in `src/main/java/practice/StockExport.java`: the header, then one line per item in the order given, with `"\n"` between lines. A catalogue with no items still gets its header.

cases.says: the file holds the header and then one line per item, in the order given
a catalogue of 40,000 items is built without copying the text so far for every line
lines are separated by a newline, and there is none after the last line
an empty catalogue gives the header line alone, with no newline after it

origin.section: Repeated Text Goes into One Buffer, and a Joiner Places the Separators

concepts: Collectors.joining writes its prefix and suffix even for no elements; StringJoiner.setEmptyValue gives the empty case its own text.
Repeated text is built in one StringBuilder or by a joiner, and a joiner writes separators only between items.
+= on a String in a loop copies everything built so far on every pass, so allocation grows with the square of the item count.
